name: Polypropylene glycol diamine
description: Polypropylene glycol diamine (CAS 9046-10-0 ) is a difunctional amine-terminated polyether used as a reactive building block in polymer systems. Its terminal amine groups enable direct participation in curing and crosslinking reactions. This versatile chemical is essential for chain extension across a broad range of thermoset and elastomeric applications. In epoxy coating systems, it acts as a flexible curing agent, improving impact resistance and elongation. It is widely utilized in protective and floor coatings to enhance durability. Polyurethane and polyurea formulations use it as a chain extender to tune mechanical properties and processing characteristics in spray-applied membranes. Adhesive manufacturers incorporate it into structural and elastic bonding systems where controlled flexibility is required. It ensures superior substrate adhesion and performance in demanding industrial environments. In construction composites and grouts, it contributes to toughened resin matrices with improved crack resistance. This makes it ideal for applications subject to dynamic loads and environmental stress over time. The product is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid available across a range of molecular weights. These typically range from 230 to 4000 g/mol, which determines the amine equivalent and reactivity. The molecular weight directly influences the flexibility and curing speed in the final system.
